newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax, Staples said resuming talk.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax, Staples said resuming talk.

text.p: OfficeMax has resumed negotiations to acquire dozens of stores from Staples, sources close to the talks said Tuesday.

If the negotiations for Staples to divest stores to OfficeMax are successful, which could take weeks, the deal could lead to government approval of the merger between Staples and Office Depot by the Federal Trade Commission.

The OfficeMax negotiations had broken down over a dispute about which stores would change hands, with money also an issue. In the absence of a divestiture agreement, the FTC rejected the Staples-Office Depot merger.

The FTC had required a divestiture of 62 stores by Staples to do the 1,000-plus store deal. Staples took the proposal to OfficeMax, which accepted 52 of the stores but wanted 20 others of its own choosing.
Staples wanted $150 million to $160 million for the mix of stores it was offering, while OfficeMax was willing to pay only $100 million for the more than 70 stores it wanted to purchase.
Given those problems, the negotiations broke down and the FTC acted.
The mix of stores which Staples offered to divest had been worked out through painstaking negotiations with the government.

Even as wheels started to turn for a series of court actions that the FTC intends will spell the end to the merger, an official at the FTC said the door remains open to negotiations that could lead to a completed deal between Staples and Office Depot.

All sides are now working against a major deadline, which has not yet been set: A court hearing for a permanent injunction against the merger. Such a hearing, before a Federal District Court judge, is expected anywhere from one week to a month or two months from now.

If the government wins a preliminary injunction from a federal judge at that hearing, and sustains the win on appeal, an official at Staples said any chance of a merger would be over. At the same time, Staples says it believes it can win in court.
